groups.title: PJM show cause proceeding (E-7)
groups.about: The E-7 order asks whether PJM’s tariff stays just and reasonable without large-load rules on the five reforms. Everything filed in EL26-67 since June 18: the 30-day report, abeyance requests and the order granting them, answers and comments.

link.text: This is the E-7 docket itself. PJM and its transmission owners must defend the tariff or file changes; after abeyance, responses are due Nov 16, 2026.

groups.title: Filed in several show cause dockets
groups.about: Interventions, comments and motions that one party filed in more than one of the six show cause dockets.

link.text: Each of these was filed in two or more of the six show cause dockets, so it answers several orders at once.

groups.title: PJM co-location compliance
groups.about: Co-location means a large load, usually a data center, built at a power plant and served partly by it. FERC set rules for it in PJM; these filings carry them out.
groups.status: PJM filed partial compliance Aug 17, 2026 and answered three limited protests Oct 14. The rest of its compliance is due Nov 16.

link.text: E-2, decided the same day as the six orders, finalized PJM’s three co-location transmission services; the six orders point to them as the model. PJM’s compliance filing is due Nov 16, alongside E-7.

groups.title: PJM Large Load definition, Registry and Interim Resource Adequacy Service
groups.about: PJM asked FERC to define a Large Load, keep a registry of them, and create a service that would curtail such loads first in a supply emergency. FERC kept the definition and the registry and rejected the rest.
groups.status: PJM filed compliance and Ohio requested rehearing on Nov 9. FERC set comments on compliance for Nov 30 at 5 p.m. Eastern.

link.text: Defines which PJM loads count as large and how PJM learns about them, which every application and study rule in E-7 depends on. Filed under section 205, outside EL26-67.

groups.title: PJM Reliability Backstop Procurement
groups.about: PJM, the grid operator for 13 states and D.C., proposed a backstop purchase of new power plants to cover a projected supply shortfall as large loads grow. On Sep 29 FERC accepted it for filing, suspended it to Feb 28, 2027 subject to refund, and set three cost issues for a paper hearing.
groups.status: FERC suspended the procurement on Sep 29. PJM filed amendments Oct 29 and refiled the same proposal Nov 9 under the §205 code in ER27-454-000. Comments are due Nov 30 at 5 p.m. Eastern.

link.text: PJM’s July 20 E-7 adequacy report presents this procurement, begun before the order, as its main resource-adequacy effort.

groups.title: Rehearing of FERC's PJM Reliability Backstop Procurement order
groups.about: Seven parties ask FERC to reconsider its September order accepting PJM's backstop procurement. Asking for rehearing is the required step before a party can take an order to court.
groups.status: Seven requests, filed Oct 13 to Oct 29, 2026. FERC had not ruled on any as of Nov 9.

link.text: Challenges to FERC’s September order on the backstop procurement, which PJM’s E-7 adequacy report presents as its main resource-adequacy effort.

groups.title: Exelon complaint seeking a prompt PJM capacity auction
groups.about: Exelon, whose utilities serve more than 10.7 million customers in PJM, asks FERC to run PJM's capacity auction two months before each delivery year instead of three years ahead.
groups.status: Filed Nov 3, 2026. Exelon asks for an order by Jan 31, 2027; FERC had not acted as of Nov 9.

link.text: A separate section 206 complaint on capacity-auction timing; it bears on the resource-adequacy topic of E-7’s 30-day report.

groups.title: MISO Large Load Addition Resource Study (LARS)
groups.about: MISO, the grid operator for 15 states in the Midwest and South, wants to study a new load of 200 MW or more together with the power plant built to serve it, in about 120 days and outside its multi-year generator queue.
groups.status: MISO answered protests on Nov 9 and asked FERC to accept LARS. The requested effective date is Dec 2.

link.text: MISO is answering E-8 in separate section 205 filings. LARS studies a large load and the generation built to serve it together, MISO’s answer to the order’s proximate-generation item.

groups.title: MISO zero-injection generator interconnection agreement
groups.about: MISO proposed a generator interconnection agreement for generation that serves on-site load and injects nothing into the grid. FERC staff found the filing deficient on Oct 9 and asked for more information.
groups.status: FERC staff issued a deficiency letter on Oct 9, 2026.

link.text: A MISO section 205 filing for generation that serves on-site load and injects nothing into the grid. It creates no new transmission service; MISO lists it among its pieces answering E-8.

groups.title: MISO interconnection reliability requirements for large loads
groups.about: MISO proposed reliability requirements that large loads must meet to connect. State regulators, consumer advocates and clean-energy groups protested; data centers, industrial customers and municipal utilities answered.
groups.status: Answers through Nov 3, 2026; no FERC order as of Nov 12.

link.text: MISO says this filing is responsive to concerns raised in EL26-70: the ongoing operating requirements a large load must meet once connected, E-8’s first item.

groups.title: SPP conditional large-load service credits (CHILLS)
groups.about: SPP proposed revenue credits for conditional large-load service in its western zones, then corrected one rate sheet on Nov 10.

link.text: SPP extends CHILLS, the conditional large-load service E-9 builds on, to its West Region. The filing does not cite E-9 or EL26-68.

groups.title: Duke Energy Carolinas network service agreement and large-load shortfall payments
groups.about: Duke Energy Carolinas' network service agreement adds a payment from customers of 100 MW or more who use less transmission than they committed to.

link.text: A non-RTO utility writing minimum-charge protections for large loads into a network service agreement, the same cost-shift protection the orders ask RTOs to consider.

groups.title: 2026 FERC reliability technical conference: integrating large loads
groups.about: FERC's annual reliability conference, run by the commissioners. Its first panel covered running the grid with fast-growing large loads such as data centers.
groups.status: Held Oct 21, 2026, with Panel 1 on integrating large loads.

link.text: FERC’s technical conference on integrating large loads reliably, including the flexible operation the orders’ new services depend on.

groups.title: PJM governance and stakeholder reform vote
groups.about: After FERC's July conference on how PJM makes decisions, PJM's members voted on a reform package. PJM told FERC the states do not find the result satisfactory.
groups.status: PJM reported the Members' Sept 30, 2026 vote to FERC on Oct 1. The Board has not said what it will file.

link.text: PJM governance reform runs beside the orders: who decides PJM’s section 205 filings, including its E-7 response.

groups.title: PJM stakeholder record on its show cause response
groups.about: Documents from PJM’s own stakeholder process as it prepared its show cause response: Members Committee agendas, the legal report and a letter from large customers to the PJM Board.
groups.status: PJM called a special Members Committee for Nov 5, 2026.

link.text: The stakeholder process PJM ran before deciding what to file in response to E-7 by Nov 16.

groups.title: Senate oversight hearing on FERC, July 22, 2026
groups.about: Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee oversight hearing with the FERC commissioners, including questions on the large-load orders.

link.text: Commissioners explained the June orders to Congress, under questioning about cost, timing and state authority.
